findings.input: new ForeignTokenRegistry([{ name: "acme", pattern: /ACME_[A-Z0-9_]+/g }]).namespaceOf("ACME_ABCDEF_0001") called repeatedly
findings.config: foreign registry with a pattern-registered namespace whose RegExp carries the g (or y) flag
findings.expected_invariant: The same registration must yield the same ownership verdict on every call, and classifyOwnership / ctx.isProtectedToken / the forward path must agree with each other. Registry contract: a registered foreign token is PRESERVED on the input path.
findings.observed: namespaceOf alternates acme/null/acme/null because RegExp.prototype.test on a g or y matcher advances lastIndex; classifyOwnership resets lastIndex before matching while isProtectedToken does not, so the two layers fight over one matcher object. Consequence: DB_PASSWORD=ACME_ABCDEF_0001 is redacted to DB_PASSWORD=CRG_... instead of being preserved, and the verdict depends on call order.
findings.impact: ownership/policy inconsistency + deployment correctness. A shared registry built once at startup gives different results than one built per request. No confidentiality leak: the failure direction is over-redaction. An EXACT registration is unaffected.
findings.control: an equivalent non-stateful matcher (/ACME_[A-Z0-9_]+/) preserves the token correctly, which locates the defect in how the matcher is used rather than in the registry's purpose
